description: The Number System is the fundamental basis of Mathematics. It involves the detailed study of types of numbers, their properties, and various mathematical operations.

sections.title: Classification of Numbers
sections.description: Numbers are divided into various categories based on their mathematical properties.

key_concepts.explanation: All counting numbers are called natural numbers. Example: 1, 2, 3, ...
If zero is included with natural numbers, they become whole numbers. Example: 0, 1, 2, 3, ...
All positive numbers, negative numbers, and zero together form integers. Example: ..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ...
Numbers that can be expressed in the form of p/q, where p and q are integers and q is not equal to zero (q != 0).
Numbers that have exactly two factors - 1 and the number itself. Example: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11

sections.title: Divisibility Rules
sections.description: These rules help determine whether a number is completely divisible by another number without performing actual division.

results: For 2: The last digit must be even or 0, 2, 4, 6, 8.
For 4: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 4.
For 8: The number formed by the last three digits must be divisible by 8.
For 3: The sum of the digits of the number must be divisible by 3.
For 9: The sum of the digits of the number must be divisible by 9.
The difference between the sum of digits at even places and the sum of digits at odd places must be either 0 or a multiple of 11.

sections.title: Unit Digit Concept
sections.description: Methods to find the last digit of a number with a large power or a large product.

key_concepts.explanation: The pattern of repetition of a number's unit digit as its power increases is called cyclicity.

steps.title: Divide the Power
steps.detail: Divide the given power of the number by 4.

steps.title: Find Remainder
steps.detail: Find the remainder. If the remainder is 0, assume the new power for calculation is 4.

steps.title: Calculate Unit Digit
steps.detail: Apply this remainder as the power to the last digit of the base number to get the final result.

results: The unit digit will always remain unchanged, regardless of the power.
For 4: If the power is odd, the unit digit is 4, and if even, it is 6.
For 9: If the power is odd, the unit digit is 9, and if even, it is 1.

sections.title: Remainder Theorem
sections.description: Important rules for finding the remainder when one number is divided by another, without using long division.

key_concepts.explanation: This concept is used only to make calculations easier. Actual Positive Remainder = Divisor - Magnitude of Negative Remainder.

sections.title: Factors
sections.description: All possible numbers that divide a given number completely are called its factors.

key_concepts.explanation: Representing a number (N) as the product of powers of prime numbers, where a, b, and c are prime bases.
